title: Collectables - Brain in a Jar Guide
subtitle: How to start {quest} in Skyline Valley, what Dr. Regina Marcs wants with all those brains, how the hand-ins and the finale work, and every reward for collecting all {total} Brains in Jars.

intro.title: How to Start {quest}
intro.html:
Brains in Jars are glass containers with a brain floating inside. There are {total} of them: {regions}. You don't need to do anything to start the quest. The first time you pick one up, your Pip-Boy picks up a signal with coordinates to a "recall" location and {quest} starts with the objective Find the source of the signal.

Step 1 – Pick up any Brain in a Jar

Any brain will do. Each jar makes a beeping noise that gets louder the closer you get, so listen out for it, and at night the jars glow green, which makes them easier to spot in the dark. Pick one up and a message pops up: your Pip-Boy has registered a set of coordinates, some sort of recall signal. This also completes the lifetime challenge Find your first Brain in a Jar. The location pages follow one route that starts at Brain in a Jar 1, Three Ponds, but that is only the recommended starting point.

Step 2 – Follow the signal to Rapidan Camp

The coordinates lead to Rapidan Camp in Skyline Valley, and specifically to the Brown House. Fast travel to Rapidan Camp, follow the quest marker to the Brown House and go inside.

Step 3 – Speak to the Ghoul

Inside is a Ghoul who isn't pleased to see you and warns you she's armed. Talk to her and she soon notices the brain jar you're carrying. She is Dr. Regina Marcs, and she's collecting the brains.

Step 4 – Make the deal

Hand over your brain and Marcs gives you a new weapon, the V63-Z Custom, a two-handed blade she calls "very fancy chopping power". She promises upgrades for it and recordings decoded from the brains if you keep bringing more. From here the objective is Collect brains in jars, then Return brain jars to Marcs.

sections.title: Handing In Brains to Dr. Marcs
sections.html:
Marcs takes the brains in {batch_count} batches. Each batch is bigger than the last, and the quest objective shows how many you still need for the next one. Finishing the quest takes {quest_brains} brains in total, so you don't need all {total} for the quest itself.

{batch_table}

Every time you hand in a batch, Marcs pays you some caps and gives you a holotape she has decoded from the brains. There are {holotape_count} of these Scan holotapes in total, listed further down. Listen as you go: they tell the story of where the brains came from and what Marcs is really after.

Each brain you pick up is worth a base of {pickup_xp} XP. Brains in Jars can't be dropped, traded or sold.

sections.title: The Finale (spoilers)
sections.html:
When you hand in the final batch, Marcs asks you to help her open a bunker hidden below the Brown House. She says the man inside may have gone feral, so expect a fight. You can say no and walk away with your rewards, but she makes it clear there's a bonus if you escort her down.

Step 1 – Get the last tape

Agree to help and Marcs gives you the last holotape she decoded. It's a set of song lyrics, and it's the key to the bunker.

Step 2 – Follow Marcs downstairs

Tell her you're ready and follow her down to the bunker door. Marcs says the password is 565 characters long, the length of the song's lyrics without spaces or punctuation. She types it in for you and the door opens.

The password, if you want to see it:

{password_block}

Step 3 – Find Iggy

The man inside is Iggy Stolz, and he's already dead. Ask Marcs about it and the truth comes out: she shot him herself after he stole her weather machine plans, and he crawled down here before he died.

Step 4 – Deal with Marcs

Marcs wants to tie up loose ends, and you're one of them. The quest then turns into Kill Marcs or Flee the Brown House. Some answers in the conversation let you talk your way out of it; most end in a fight. Either way, finishing the quest pays {caps} caps, XP and a Skyline Valley loot roll.

Dialogue checks

There are no Charisma checks in A Matter of Matter. These are the only special answers in the conversations with Marcs:

  • [PER 12+] – "This isn't adding up. You're hiding something." Needs Perception 12 or more. Marcs admits she and Iggy were planning to steal the weather machine plans together.
  • [Enclave] – "Wait... you mean the Enclave? I'm a member, too." Only if you have finished One of Us. Marcs lets you say a few more words before the fight.
  • [Ghoul] – "To do whatever it takes to survive as one of us..." Only if you are a Ghoul, when she asks what your role is. She calls a truce.

sections.html: Finishing {quest} unlocks the {camp_name} for your CAMP. It costs {camp_cost}, and you can place up to 10 of them.

sections.title: The Story Behind the Brains (spoilers)
sections.html:
Marcs was once Lieutenant Regina Marcs of Vault 63, where she led the weather manipulation research for a time, trading the job back and forth with Audrey Stolz. She came to Vault 63 from Atlas Observatory, along with Oberlin.

The brains come from a "Brain Bleaching" operation the Stolz family ran on the west coast, at Chez Alpine: Spa and Resort. Rich and famous guests, mostly from the film industry, were treated there by the "world-renowned Dr. Scheinmenn", and the recordings show Iggy Stolz interviewing them. Iggy was Hugo Stolz's adopted son, raised as the heir until Audrey was born.

Iggy was hunting for a secret in the brains: a musical called Sonny, O' My Boy that he believed Hugo had written for him. Marcs, meanwhile, wanted her own improved version of the weather machine plans, which Iggy stole. She decoded the brains to find the password Iggy set on the bunker, and in the end she tells you she is "an agent of America. The real one."

locations_html: The brains are split into pages in route order. Every page has the route map and the full maps in its Maps section, at the bottom of the page.
milestones_html: Lifetime challenges count every Brain in a Jar you find, whether or not you are doing the quest. faq.title: FAQ and Important Info
faq.html:
Do I have to do the quest to get the lifetime rewards?

No. The lifetime challenges count every brain you find, all the way to {total}. The quest only needs {quest_brains} brains handed in to Marcs.

How much XP is each brain worth?

A base of {pickup_xp} XP every time you pick one up.

Can I give spare brains to a friend?

No, your friend is beyond help, sorry. Plus, Brains in Jars can't be dropped, traded or sold.

Is there a way to find the brains without a guide?

Yes. Every jar makes a beeping noise that gets louder the closer you get to it, and at night the jars glow green, so they stand out in the dark. Follow the beeping, or go looking after dark.

How do I start the questline?

Pick up any Brain in a Jar. There's nothing to do first: the first jar you pick up starts A Matter of Matter.
